subject: Post-call recap: Radiant Health integration priorities & technical gaps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <e.carter@radianthealth.com>, Dr. Sanjay Patel <s.patel@radianthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 20:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: Radiant Health integration priorities & technical gaps

Hi Emily / Sanjay —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned and to capture the technical gaps we should address before a pilot. I’ve kept this short and added owners / timelines. Attached: a first-pass integration diagram and a mutual action plan workbook.

High-level goals you shared
- Reduce clinical triage time by surfacing structured summaries and recommended follow-ups inside EHR workflows.
- Maintain strict PHI controls and data locality for B2B patient-facing notes.
- Keep token costs predictable for the high-volume triage flow (peak hours).

Top pain points called out
1) Latency on live triage (~500–700ms target per reply) during peak shifts; current vendor pipeline is inconsistent.
2) Need for function-calling hooks to call internal triage services (patient lookup, rule-based triage fallback).
3) Streaming partial responses into the UI (progressive rendering) while also supporting structured JSON outputs for downstream automation.
4) Embedding-based reranking for clinician search results across notes and care plans.
5) Data residency + KMS integration for audit logs and encryption keys.

Technical fit summary (what Redwood can provide)
- SDK: lightweight JS + Python adapters; will add a function-calling sample that shows a secure call to your triage microservice with token scoping. Owner: Laura. ETA: prototype in 5 business days.
- Streaming: continuous chunked responses + prefix caching to hit your 500ms p50 under our recommended batching config. Owner: Sergio. ETA: test harness by next Wed.
- Structured output: schema-first generation with automatic validation hooks (we’ll propose a small JSON schema for the triage summary). Owner: Mina. ETA: initial schema draft in 3 business days.
- Embeddings / rerank: recommended model family + quantization profile; we’ll provide a warm-start index and scoring thresholds to avoid regressions. Owner: Ben. ETA: benchmark report in 7 business days.
- Compliance: outline for VPC private deployment, KMS/HSM integration details and sample audit logs. Owner: Mina & Security.

Open questions (need your input)
- Which EHR environment(s) will the pilot target (Epic / Cerner / proprietary)?
- Expected daily active sessions and peak QPS for triage microflow?
- Do you have any existing embedding vectors / search indexes we should align on, or should Redwood start fresh?

Next concrete steps
1) Laura to share SDK function-calling sample (internal) — 2026-12-23 — Laura Bennett
2) Sergio to provide streaming test harness + config recommendations — 2026-12-23 — Sergio Alvarez
3) Ben to run an embedding/rerank benchmark using your sample dataset (if you provide) or synthetic fallback — 2026-12-25 — Ben Carter
4) Mina to circulate a short MAP (attached) and a proposed pilot schedule — 2026-12-19 — Mina Haddad

If the above looks right I’ll schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45 mins) to walk through the diagram and agree on pilot acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0191

Attachments: radiant_integration_diagram_v1.png (diagram), RADIANT-MAP-MutualActionPlan.xlsx (MAP workbook)

From: Emily Carter <e.carter@radianthealth.com>

Cc: Dr. Sanjay Patel <s.patel@radianthealth.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@radianthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 22:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Radiant Health integration priorities & technical gaps

Thanks Mina — useful summary. A few clarifications:

- Pilot EHR: we’ll run the first pilot inside Epic (testing environment) and then a second small pilot in our proprietary ambulatory app.
- Peak QPS: expect ~1200 QPS during morning triage windows across all hospitals (that’s our rough current load).
- Embeddings: we have a pre-existing clinical-notes embedding index (S3) that we’d prefer to reuse if the vector dimensions match. I will share access details in a follow-up secure transfer.

Could you also add a section in the MAP that explicitly lists data flows for PHI vs de-identified behavior? Our security team needs that for SOC2 evidence.

When you send the SDK sample, please include an example of scoped API keys (short-lived) and how Redwood surfaces audit log entries.

Appreciate the timeline — please add a tentative date/time for the technical deep-dive (we prefer morning PT).

—Emily
Emily Carter
Head of Clinical Integrations, Radiant Health
e.carter@radianthealth.com | +1 212-555-0147
